To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of malignant cells in liver tissue causes alterations in the occurrence and expression of basement membrane proteins and integrin chains in hepatic microcirculatory system.
the presence of metastases is associated with the enhanced expression of basement membrane proteins, and integrins, and with the occurrence of α-SMA-positive cells in the liver.

the expression of basement membrane proteins, collagen type IV laminin and integrins, α1 and α 6, is increased in sinusoids of the liver in the presence of metastases, and that the metastatic tumour cells can adhere to laminin deposits in sinusoids.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the possible mechanisms involved in liver metastases development.
the expression of basement membrane proteins and integrin chains in livers with metastases, and their potential roles in the metastatic process.
a possible role of HSCs in the formation and growth of liver metastases, which might have important therapeutic implications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of collagen type IV, α1 and α 6 integrin chains, laminin and αSMA is altered in the liver with malignant metastases, and this may be related to the metastatic process.
the metastatic cells induce changes in the liver microenvironment, and these alterations might contribute to the development of liver metastases.

in the liver with malignant tumour metastases, the occurrence of basement membrane proteins and integrin chains in metastases and in sinusoids is altered and that this might contribute to the further dissemination of metastatic tumour cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the metastatic cells can produce stimuli that induce sinusoidal changes and the activation of HSCs, which in turn may facilitate the further dissemination of metastases.
the metastatic liver tissue is a complex organ with a unique extracellular matrix, which can profoundly affect the behaviour of metastatic cancer cells.
metastatic cells can use the extracellular matrix proteins, which are normally present in the liver, for their further dissemination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of laminin and integrins can be used as a prognostic marker in patients with liver metastases from malignant tumours.
the basement membrane proteins, collagen type IV in the space of the Disse, and laminin, are important in metastatic cell attachment to the extracellular matrix.
the basement membrane proteins and integrin chains expression is altered in the liver with malignant tumours, and the expression is associated with tumour progression and metastases.
